name: Yaben
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page yabe1255 (live, 2026-09-17) and held hh.bib
sources.note: Refs: Pick 2020 (subclassification, pp. 188-194, 397-398) + Ethnologue 2025; zero descriptive references. hh.bib: Yaben [ybm] only in Z'graggen survey language code lists; 'Yaben' MA theses are Konda [knd].

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Yaben = F16; ~300-item semi-phonemic wordlist. Intro sec. 7 (p. viii): 'The transcription is rendered semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; fluctuation table only; the word 'stress' does not occur in the front matter; Yaben forms carry no stress marks (checked on the p. 4 image: tʌ, tiña, uda 'father'; niña, unʌd 'mother').

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Comparative tables with F16 Yaben forms (ubatu 'arm', gunu 'nose', nu 'egg'); population table Yaben 702; no stress/accent/tone remark anywhere.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU.http://hdl.handle.net/1885/130077
sources.note: Printed p. 13 (p. 22): same sentence, 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Superseded by the 1971 published version.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 486 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32): stress described only for Mauwake (Berghall 2015: 42), Pamosu (Tupper 2012: 99-102) and Usan (Reesink 1987: 39-40); 'the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. Sec. 4.3 Yaben (pp. 154-157; 4.3.1 phonemes pp. 155-156, based on Z'graggen's JZ2 recordings): 4 V /i u ə a/, 13 C, /k/ often glottal stop, epenthetic final u, /a/~/ə/ contrast; no mention of stress, accent, tone or pitch. Sec. 10.5 Sound changes in Yaben (pp. 424-425): segmental only.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2019. Yamben: a previously undocumented language of Papua New Guinea. In M. Suzuki (ed.), 2018 Proceedings: Selected papers from the 22nd college-wide conference for students in LLL, 25-35. Honolulu: UH Manoa. handle 10125/63092
sources.note: p. 25: 'Yaben itself is also poorly documented, with Z'graggen's (1980) wordlist being the only published data on the language that I am aware of.' Yaben appears only in the 20-item comparative table (data from Z'graggen 1980); the phonology section concerns Yamben, not Yaben; nothing on Yaben stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: p. 6 (p. 14), whole-survey remark: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sec. 2.22.24.12 Yaben 32/Ya (480 speakers; villages Idimakuma, Gulkrubrana, Barata, Abaiya, Magilan; 'First listed by Kasprus (1942)'); Wayapan Family typological notes p. 54 list segmental phonemes and possessive-class type only. Nothing on Yaben stress.

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org/language/yaben; Wikipedia 'Yaben language'; UH ScholarSpace search 'Yaben'; ANU Open Research search 'Yaben'
sources.note: TransNewGuinea: 364 items from Z'graggen 1980 and Pick 2019, no phonology; Wikipedia: stub; ScholarSpace: only Pick 2020 and the 2019 proceedings; ANU: only the Z'graggen items above. Nothing on stress.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6621.U77 R4 x, 1987
sources.note: Grammar of Usan (wanu1241), Yaben's closest relative (63% cognate per Z'graggen 1971); its stress description (phonemic stress, minimal pairs) is the nearest available analogue and would guide any listening analysis of the Yaben recordings. Not a Yaben source; relevant to a different catalog entry.
